text.text:
The two lookups, as text

With shop 10, the order reference asks for (10, 103), and finds Mina’s order. The product reference asks for (10, P7), and finds the Blue mug. Both references are satisfied.

With shop 20, the product reference asks for (20, P7), and finds the Copper mug. The order reference asks for (20, 103), which is absent. Order (10, 103) cannot satisfy it, so the order foreign key refuses the attempted line.

text.text:
All outcomes as text

With no change, both methods return 103 and 105. After 101 is cancelled, OFFSET 2 returns 105 and 106, skipping 103; the saved key returns 103 and 105. If 103’s time moves to 13 October 12:00 UTC, the list becomes 101, 103, 102, 105, 106. OFFSET 2 repeats 102 and returns 105. The saved key returns 105 and 106, but misses the moved 103. These are independent illustrative histories, with cancelled orders excluded from the list.

The complete schedule as text

First, the reader gets 101 and 102. A separate writer then cancels 103 and commits. A new statement snapshot sees only 101, 102, 105 and 106; continuing after 102 returns 105 and 106. With one fixed snapshot established before that commit, the reader still sees all five original rows; continuing after 102 returns 103 and 105. The writer’s change committed in either case. This illustration concerns ordinary reads, without row locks.

text.text:
Read the paths as text

Success: borrow C, begin, reserve stock and write order, commit, return idle C. No stock: borrow, begin, receive zero rows, roll back all earlier work, return idle C. Statement cancelled: borrow, begin, receive cancellation error, roll back the failed transaction, return idle C. Connection lost: borrow, begin, lose the connection, discard C, resolve any uncertain commit separately before retrying the purchase.
